Ten days, 14 to 24 June 2024, anticlockwise on Route 1 with Leonor. The route itself is 1,332 km, but with detours
the odometer said 2,180 km when we handed the keys back. It never got dark once.

## The vehicle

Dacia Duster 4x4 from Bláfell Rentals at Keflavík, booking BFR-60417. ISK 19,800 a day. Added gravel protection for
ISK 2,900 a day, which paid for itself: a stone chipped the windscreen on day 6 near Egilsstaðir and we were charged
zero. The contract banned F-roads, so the highlands stay on the wishlist. I photographed every scratch at the pickup
bay, 23 photos, and the agent rolled his eyes.

## Fuel and money

Prepaid fuel cards from N1 and Orkan, ISK 10,000 each. Petrol was around ISK 330 a litre. Total fuel spend ISK
61,500. The pumps want a PIN: my Revolut card worked, Leonor's didn't, so the fuel cards saved us twice in the east.

## South coast, days 1 to 3

- Seljalandsfoss: you walk behind the waterfall, wear a rain jacket, I didn't
- Skógafoss: 527 steps up the side, counted them out loud
- Reynisfjara black sand: the sea grabs people there, we stayed well back
- Slept at Bláberg guesthouse in Vík, ISK 24,000 a night with breakfast

## Glacier lagoon

Jökulsárlón at 23:30 in full daylight, icebergs drifting out to sea and washing up on the black sand across the road.
Skipped the paid tour (ISK 9,900 each) and just sat on the shore with a thermos. Seals popping up every few minutes.

## East fjords

Seyðisfjörður and its rainbow street, fog so thick we couldn't see the mountains for a whole day. Loads of
single-lane bridges: whoever reaches the bridge first goes, flash your lights to say thanks.

## Mývatn and the north

Mývatn Nature Baths, ISK 6,490 each, cheaper and calmer than the Blue Lagoon. Hverir mud pots smell like rotten eggs
and the colours look fake. Akureyri has the famous hot dog debate; Leonor says Bæjarins Beztu, I say the stand at
the Akureyri N1. Neither of us is right.

## Westfjords, skipped

Not enough days. Next time 14 days minimum and only the west.

## Food costs

Bónus supermarket (the pink pig logo) kept us alive: skyr ISK 289, rye bread, smoked lamb. Splurged on lamb soup at
Súpustofan in Höfn, ISK 2,450, refills included.

## Afterwards

A year later the [[Road trip Scotland]] felt tiny in comparison, but the single-track etiquette was exactly the same.
Checked a 23 kg bag this time; the [[Packing list carry-on]] would never have covered rain gear for ten days.
